title: HEO Unveils Insights Next SDA Tool
html:
If a picture is worth a thousand words, then Australian non-Earth imaging (NEI) startup HEO has a lot to say about the state of orbital traffic.

The company unveiled a new intelligence tool—called Insights Next—aiming to give satellite operators and defense organizations a more robust understanding of what’s happening across the space domain. The platform puts HEO’s non-Earth imagery into a 3D visualization, giving users the ability to understand what an object is doing on-orbit, where its sensors are pointing, and how its behavior is changing.

“Insights Next is an important step in our vision for how space intelligence should be delivered,” HEO cofounder and CEO Will Crowe said in a statement. “We’ve spent years building the infrastructure to image objects across orbit, on demand. The next step is connecting those observations with the information needed to make sense of activity in space.”

User guide: Insights Next is built on a foundation of 7,500+ NEI missions covering 1,200 unique space objects, which HEO has amassed from its network of 50+ sensors on orbit. The platform combines these images with spatial context and object information to add a frame of reference on top of the imagery.

The platform will allow users to understand an object’s “position relative to Earth, orientation, dimensions, payload configuration and pointing direction alongside the original observation,” according to the announcement.

The new tool comes online during a high-growth phase for HEO, which is experiencing an upswell in the amount and quality of NEI data it’s gathering.

  • The company raised a $25M Series B in September to expand its imaging network to GEO, and kickstart an effort to monitor 90% of all space objects in orbit. Crowe told Payload the company expects to cross 10,000 missions by the end of next year.
  • HEO reported a 3x increase in revenue year-over-year, accelerated by an expansion of its international footprint, and a new effort to sell hardware and software to allied governments for sovereign capabilities.
  • HEO also made improvements to its HEO Inspect platform, adding AI-backed automation to its sensor tasking, detection, and analysis of imagery.

The goal for Insights Next is to house all of this new imagery alongside relevant contextual data, to give analysts the ability to assess situations and act on them—quicker than a simple photo ever could.

“It is the foundation for a more connected intelligence environment, where every observation contributes to a deeper understanding of the space domain, ultimately helping customers get to the answers they need faster and with greater confidence,” Crowe said.
